title: Non-blocking follow-up from backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups-followups's PR #357 review
description: PR #357 (backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups-followups-followups) closed out PR #355's 6 non-blocking findings (eager find_swing_points guard, latest_divergence/current_divergence tie-break dedup with a mutation-tested and coverage-gap-closing refactor, test fixture dedup, and 3 append-only decisions corrections on two ancestor tasks) and was accepted after independent re-verification (own mutation test, own pre-existing-coverage-gap re-derivation via an origin/main worktree, own ancestor-task diffs, independently re-run tests/coverage/static-analysis/task-board-validation). This tracks the review's non-blocking findings so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #357 review finding: after this PR's refactor (`latest_divergence` now delegates to `_latest_divergence_from_swings` instead of calling `find_divergences` directly), `find_divergences` (backend/app/signals/divergence.py, module-level, public) has zero callers anywhere in `app/` -- confirmed via grep, no production call site remains (it's exercised only by `tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py`). This is a pre-existing condition, not newly introduced by this PR: `current_divergence` (the only production caller of anything in this module, via `app.signals.engine.analyse`) never called `latest_divergence` even before PR #357 (it already computed swing points directly since the PR #354/#355 swing-sharing optimization), and `latest_divergence` itself already had zero production callers per this task's own ancestor-task decisions-entry correction (item 5 of the parent task's checklist) -- `find_divergences` was already unreachable from production before this PR simply followed the same chain one level further. Worth a documentation pass: either note in `find_divergences`'s own docstring (and/or a `decisions` entry on the task that introduced it, `backend-divergence-detection`) that it and `latest_divergence` are both now test-only/reference public functions with no production call site, or reconsider whether they should still be public API surface at all.

PR #357 review finding (backgrounded code-review skill pass, high effort): the `_FIXTURE_B_PRICE`/`_FIXTURE_B_MACD_HISTOGRAM` module-level comment this PR added (`tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py`, near line 91) claims 'every other `current_divergence` test in this file exercises the bullish/lows side only' -- but this same PR also adds `test_current_divergence_agrees_with_latest_divergence_on_a_two_candidate_fixture`, which calls `current_divergence` on `_FIXTURE_C_*` and asserts `result.kind == "bearish"`, i.e. it also exercises `current_divergence`'s bearish/highs-selecting path (via the multi-candidate tie-break, a different branch than FIXTURE_B's single-candidate bearish-only branch, but still a bearish `current_divergence` result). The comment's claim was accurate for the PRE-#357 file but became stale the moment this PR's own FIXTURE_C test was added alongside it. Cosmetic, self-inflicted by this PR -- worth a small wording fix (e.g. 'every other single-candidate `current_divergence` test...') next time this file is touched.

PR #357 review finding (backgrounded code-review skill pass, high effort): `latest_divergence`'s refactored body calls `swing_lows(price, window=window)` and `swing_highs(price, window=window)` as two separate calls, each of which independently reruns the full `find_swing_points` scan over the same `price` series (2 full O(history) passes) -- rather than one `find_swing_points` call partitioned by `kind` locally, the pattern `current_divergence`/`build_divergence_swing_cache` already use to avoid exactly this redundancy (see `docs/tasks/done/backend-swing-point-detector-followups.json`'s checklist item 4/its decisions entry, which deliberately fixed this double-scan ONLY at `build_divergence_swing_cache`, the one call site judged to `genuinely need both sides` at the time). Not a regression this PR introduces -- `latest_divergence`'s pre-#357 body had the identical 2-scan cost via two separate `find_divergences` calls (bullish then bearish), each internally hitting `swing_lows`/`swing_highs` respectively -- and `latest_divergence` has zero production callers today (see this task's other checklist items), so the cost is real only for direct/test callers of this specific public function. Worth considering whether `latest_divergence` should also do one partitioned `find_swing_points` call instead of two, next time this module is touched for a reason that would naturally include it.

decisions.decision: Documented `find_divergences`'s status in its own docstring as having no production caller today (kept as a public, test/reference-only entry point), rather than removing it or leaving the gap undocumented.
decisions.rationale: `find_divergences` is exercised extensively and directly by tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py (the module's own hand-computed reference-value tests target it as the simplest, most direct entry point for exercising every filter in `_evaluate_pair`), and the rest of the module's tie-break/caching helpers (`divergences_from_swings`, `_latest_divergence_from_swings`) are built on the same code path it exercises -- removing it would either delete that direct test coverage or force those tests onto a less direct entry point for no behavioral gain. Kept public rather than made private (`_find_divergences`) since nothing in this task's scope calls for an API-surface change, only a documentation gap fix; a future task can reconsider visibility if this status changes.

decisions.decision: Fixed `latest_divergence`'s double swing-point scan: replaced its separate `swing_lows(price, window=window)` + `swing_highs(price, window=window)` calls with a single `find_swing_points(price, window=window)` call partitioned locally by `kind`, matching the pattern `current_divergence`/`build_divergence_swing_cache` already use.
decisions.rationale: `swing_lows`/`swing_highs` are each just `find_swing_points` plus a `kind` filter (app.signals.swing_points), so calling both independently reruns the identical O(history_length) scan over the identical `price`/`window` pair twice for no behavioral difference -- verified the two approaches are equivalent by inspecting `swing_points.py` directly. The parent task's own ancestor decision (docs/tasks/done/backend-swing-point-detector-followups.json) deliberately scoped this fix to only `build_divergence_swing_cache` at the time, the one call site judged to need it then; this task's own checklist item explicitly flagged `latest_divergence` as the same pattern recurring and this task is already touching this exact function/file for two other checklist items, so 'next time this module is touched for a reason that would naturally include it' (the prior finding's own phrasing) applies now rather than deferring further. Rejected leaving it merely documented-but-unfixed: the fix is small, behavior-preserving (confirmed by the existing test suite, all of which still passes), and removes a real if narrow inefficiency rather than just restating it for a third time in the task history.

comments.summary: find_divergences's docstring now contains two adjacent, self-contradicting paragraphs: the pre-existing sentence ('fine for a single whole-history pass (e.g. GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis, or this module's own reference tests)...') reads as citing the analysis endpoint as a real usage example, while this PR's own new paragraph immediately below states plainly 'no production caller today.' Not a functional bug (confirmed via grep -rn find_divergences app/ tests/ that there is genuinely zero production call site), but confusing for a future reader deciding this function's blast radius. Non-blocking; filed as a follow-up.

review.notes: Full review: pytest 1491 passed (no regressions); coverage 100% overall and on app/signals/divergence.py (gate 90%); ruff/mypy/profit-target-wording guard all clean; frontend untouched, no UI surface on this PR so browser walkthrough and e2e suite explicitly skipped (not silently omitted). verify-elder-signal check against docs/Analyse.md Row 11: no methodology drift, this is a pure internal refactor with no change to detection algorithm/tie-break/filters. Claim 3 (latest_divergence's double-scan consolidation) independently verified: read app/signals/swing_points.py directly and confirmed swing_lows/swing_highs are each exactly find_swing_points filtered by kind, with find_swing_points pure/deterministic and SwingPoint a frozen dataclass, so a single find_swing_points call partitioned locally by kind is provably identical to two separate swing_lows/swing_highs calls. Mutation-tested by temporarily swapping the low/high filter conditions in latest_divergence's new body and rerunning tests/unit/signals/test_divergence.py: 5 of 39 tests failed immediately, confirming the suite genuinely covers this partition logic; reverted the mutation (file restored byte-for-byte, verified via git diff showing no changes) and reran to confirm 39/39 pass. Task-board bookkeeping (checklist items, decisions entries, index.json mirror) all correctly done -- no undecided 'decide X' checklist items. One non-blocking finding recorded above and tracked as a follow-up task.
